mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in a given month coincides with a decline in 20-day S&P 500 forward returns due to higher discount rates eroding expected future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative despite persistent FEDFUNDS > 4.0%; or IC > 0.05 in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in UNRATE by more than 0.2 percentage points coincides with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market tightening reduces hiring expectations and compresses corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >0.2pp in the current month
failure_condition: Across 5 consecutive months of UNRATE > 0.2pp increases, 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05); or IC < 0.10 over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real GDP) exceeds INDPRO by at least 2% in the same month, it indicates strong demand relative to supply, which is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investor confidence improves.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 - INDPRO > 2.0% in the current month
failure_condition: Over 10 out-of-sample windows where GDPC1 - INDPRO > 2%, 20-day forward returns are negative or flat (mean < 0); or IC > 0.15.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline of at least 3% in INDPRO over two consecutive months signals weakening business capacity, which predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates profit compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >3.0% in month t and again in month t+1
failure_condition: During 3 such INDPRO declines, 5-day forward returns are not negative (mean > 0); or IC < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2.0% for three consecutive months, it creates a persistent accommodative stance that is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return via equity valuation expansion.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window of accommodation, 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the prior 60-day average (p > 0.10); or IC > 0.20.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in PAYEMS of over 10,000 jobs coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak labor demand increases the risk of layoffs and dampens consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by >10,000 in the current month
failure_condition: During 4 such job losses, 20-day forward returns are not negative (mean > 0); or IC > 0.12.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly convergence of HOUST (household spending) and CPIAUCSL (inflation) to levels above 4.0% suggests a late-cycle demand surge that precedes a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: Both HOUST and CPIAUCSL exceed 4.0% in the current month
failure_condition: Across 8 such months, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05); or IC > 0.18.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 5% for two consecutive months predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals softening retail demand and margin compression.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >5.0% in month t and again in month t+1
failure_condition: During 4 such declines, 60-day forward returns are not negative (mean > 0); or IC > 0.15.
